title: Terraform modules
subtitle: Build reusable modules with clear inputs, outputs and resource addresses.

delta.before: A flat stack may have made every internal attribute feel globally available.
delta.after: Give child modules the inputs they need and read the outputs they return.

exercises.title: Scope Debugger
exercises.description: Find and fix a mix-up between root and child module values.

cases.prompt: The root tries module.app_tier.aws_vpc.app.id. What interface should it use?
choices: Expose output vpc_id in the child and use module.app_tier.vpc_id
Put the root local in a different file
cases.correct: Expose output vpc_id in the child and use module.app_tier.vpc_id
cases.explanation: A child publishes values through outputs; its resource namespace is private.

cases.prompt: A child needs a value stored in a root local.
choices: Use local.root_value from inside the child
Pass it as an input variable
Use an output block inside the child to read the root
cases.correct: Pass it as an input variable
cases.explanation: Module scope does not implicitly inherit root locals.

cases.prompt: A Git-sourced module must use release v1.2.0.
choices: Set version in the module block
cases.explanation: The version argument is for registry modules; Git uses source ref selection.

cost.assumptions: Short-lived resources, no compute, standard parameters, no uploads; gross usage before account credits.

checkpoints.prompt: Can a child directly read a local declared only in the root module?

rationale.b: Pass the value through a declared input.

checkpoints.prompt: How should the root read a child network ID?

rationale.b: Child internals are not exposed as root attributes.

checkpoints.prompt: How do registry and Git module sources select versions?

choices.a: Registry uses version; Git uses a source ref

rationale.a: The source kind determines the applicable version-selection mechanism.
rationale.b: The provider lockfile does not pin every module package.
